info.title: Nuage DB
info.summary: SQL over HTTP: any language that can send JSON can use Nuage DB.
info.description: Send SQL with `?` (or `$1`) parameters to `POST /v1/sql` with the token of an application; rows come back as JSON objects. The token picks the application's database. Several statements (separated by `;`, or in `statements`) run in one transaction, all or nothing. Parameters are never parsed as SQL. Examples in many languages: https://github.com/maxlestage/Nuage/tree/master/clients Applications and their tokens are made with the management API, `/api/apps`, and the server's NUAGE_ADMIN_TOKEN. An application's files (map tiles, photos, archives) are at `/v1/files`: the server lists them and signs links to its S3-compatible bucket, and the bytes go straight between the client and the bucket. Each application also has a key-value store in memory, the way Redis is used, at `/v1/kv`: values with an expiry, counters, locks, and the commands of Redis as JSON.

get.description: The application the token opens, its access, branch and tables. Without a token, or with one that opens nothing, a 401 says what is wrong.

example.message: Connected to Nuage DB 0.4.2: application `blog`, read and write, branch `main`, 3 table(s).

post.description: One statement answers its result; several answer `{"results": [...]}`, one result per statement. A read-only token may only read.

value.sql: SELECT id, title FROM posts WHERE category = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 20

statements.sql: UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance - ? WHERE id = ?
UPDATE accounts SET balance = balance + ? WHERE id = ?

post.summary: Add to a counter, or change an expiry
post.description: `?incr` (`=5`, `&ttl=60`) adds to a counter and answers `{"value": n}`: a key that does not exist counts from 0, and `ttl` is the expiry of a counter this call creates (a rate limit in one request). `?expire=60` makes the key expire, `?persist` makes it stay: `{"set": true}`, false when there is no such key.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The key: 1 to 1024 bytes, percent-encoded where the URL needs it (`session%3A42`, or `session:42`); it may hold `/`.

parameters.name: incr
parameters.description: What to add (1 when empty; negative to subtract).

parameters.name: ttl
parameters.description: With `incr`: the expiry, in seconds, of a counter this call creates.

parameters.name: expire
parameters.description: The key expires after this many seconds.

parameters.name: persist
parameters.description: The key never expires.

200.description: `value` for a counter, `set` for an expiry.

400.description: The value is not a whole number, or none of `incr`, `expire`, `persist`.

get.description: A `307` redirect to a signed download link: the bytes come from the bucket, which answers `Range` requests (a download resumes where it stopped) and `404` for a missing file. A read-only token downloads too.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The file's name: letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, in parts separated by `/` (`regions/fr.tar`); no `.` or `..` part. In the path it stays as it is: `/v1/files/regions/fr.tar`.

parameters.name: link
parameters.description: Present (`?link`): the link as JSON instead of a redirect, for clients that keep the `Authorization` header on redirects.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: The bucket answers with `Content-Disposition: attachment`, under this file name (the last part of the name when empty).

token.description: A token of an application (the console's Tokens tab, or NUAGE_TOKEN).

adminToken.description: The server's NUAGE_ADMIN_TOKEN (32 characters at least): it opens the management API, `/api/apps`, and nothing else.

Value.description: A value: text, number, boolean, null, or JSON.

sql.description: One statement, or several separated by `;`.

params.description: Values of the `?` (in order) or `$n` parameters.

arrays.description: Rows as arrays, in the order of `columns`, instead of objects.

kind.description: `validation` (bad SQL or values), `unique_violation`, `constraint`, `no_such_table`, `table_exists`, `conversion`, `unsupported`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden` (a read-only token writing), `not_found`, `conflict` (another commit came first: retry), `transaction_finished`, `database`; on `/api/apps`, also `method_not_allowed`; on `/v1/files`, also `not_configured` (no bucket) and `storage` (the bucket failed).

id.description: Its 8 characters after `nuage_`: enough to tell tokens apart, not to guess one.

tokens.description: Its tokens, by id: never a token itself.

origins.description: Websites whose pages may call it from the browser (CORS).

Env.description: The two lines to paste in the application's configuration.

name.description: Its name in the application's folder.

updated.description: When it was last written, as the bucket says (`2026-11-15T07:16:00.000Z`).

etag.description: Changes when the file changes (an MD5 of its bytes for a single upload).

url.description: The signed link, to the bucket itself. Send it without an `Authorization` header.

expires_at.description: The link works until then (NUAGE_FILES_LINK_MINUTES, an hour by default).

KvCommand.description: A command of Redis, its name first: `["SET", "key", "value", "EX", 60]`. Strings and counters: GET, SET (EX, PX, NX, XX, KEEPTTL, GET), SETNX, SETEX, PSETEX, GETSET, GETDEL, GETEX, MGET, MSET, MSETNX, APPEND, STRLEN, INCR, DECR, INCRBY, DECRBY, DEL, UNLINK, EXISTS, EXPIRE, PEXPIRE, TTL, PTTL, PERSIST, TYPE, KEYS, SCAN, DBSIZE, FLUSHDB, FLUSHALL, PING, ECHO, INFO.

KvReply.description: The answer of a command: text (`"OK"`, a value), a number, `null` for nothing, a list; in a list of commands, `{"error": "ERR ..."}` for one that was refused.

bytes.description: Memory the keys and values take.

max_bytes.description: The limit (NUAGE_KV_MB): past it, the least recently used keys go.

Error.description: The statement failed; nothing was changed.
